verdict.summary: You can build, install and share your app with other workspaces the same day. Commercial distribution at scale is expected to go through Slack Marketplace review, and Slack's policy bans using its data to train an LLM, which matters for agent builders.

time_to_first_connection.basis: Estimate: create app, add scopes and an HTTPS redirect URL, install to your workspace.

time_to_production.basis: Unlisted public distribution is a toggle. Marketplace review time varies with volume; Slack shows an estimate on the submission page.

top_blockers: Redirect URLs must be HTTPS, so localhost dev needs a tunnel
Marketplace review is manual and returns apps that aren't fully functional
Some scopes aren't accepted for the Marketplace

key_decision.question: Unlisted distribution or Slack Marketplace?
key_decision.recommendation: Unlisted for pilots with early customers; submit to the Marketplace before selling at scale.
key_decision.why: Slack's developer policy (updated Dec 2024) says apps intended for commercial distribution at scale should go through Marketplace review, and forbids offering a parallel unlisted app that circumvents Marketplace guidelines.

prerequisites.item: A Slack workspace where you can install apps
Public support page and fully working app

steps.title: Create the app
steps.detail: Go to api.slack.com/apps, create an app from scratch and pick a development workspace.

steps.title: Choose bot vs user token scopes
steps.detail: Bot scopes give an xoxb token for the app; user scopes give an xoxp token that acts as the installing user. Request only what your agent needs.

steps.title: Add redirect URLs
steps.detail: Under OAuth & Permissions. Must be HTTPS. The redirect_uri you send must match or be a subdirectory of a registered URL.

steps.title: Decide on token rotation before launch
steps.detail: Opt-in. When on, access tokens expire in 12 hours and need refreshing. A third-party guide says it can't be turned off once enabled.

steps.title: Install to your own workspace and run the OAuth flow
steps.detail: Use the authorize URL https://slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize with your client_id and scopes.

steps.title: Activate public distribution
steps.detail: Manage Distribution → Share Your App with Other Workspaces → Activate Public Distribution. This makes the app installable by other workspaces without being listed.

steps.title: Submit to the Slack Marketplace (for commercial scale)
steps.detail: Public distribution is a prerequisite. Review has a preliminary stage then a functional review. Submit only a bug-free, complete app.

nuances.title: No training LLMs on Slack data
nuances.detail: Slack's developer policy explicitly prohibits using data collected by your app to train an LLM. Agent products must make sure their data handling complies.

nuances.title: Coded workflows can't be listed
nuances.detail: Coded workflows are currently not eligible for the Marketplace.

nuances.title: Docs moved
nuances.detail: api.slack.com documentation now redirects to docs.slack.dev, so older links in tutorials may be stale.

blockers.symptom: Can't save a localhost redirect URL
blockers.fix: Use an HTTPS tunnel (e.g. ngrok) or a deployed preview URL.

blockers.cause: App not fully functional or uses unaccepted scopes
blockers.escalation: Slack Marketplace team via the submission page

agent_can: Map your agent's actions to the minimum bot/user scopes
Generate the app manifest and redirect URL list
Draft Marketplace listing copy and a pre-submission checklist
you_must: Create the app while signed in to Slack
Set up HTTPS hosting or a tunnel
Submit for Marketplace review and answer reviewer questions

unverified: Marketplace review duration: Slack doesn't publish a number outside the submission page.
That token rotation is irreversible comes from a third-party guide, not Slack's docs.
